metadata.title: Keystroke Dynamics Patterns While Writing Positive and Negative Opinions

abstract: This paper analyzes behavioral patterns in human-computer interaction (HCI) by examining keystroke dynamics while participants wrote positive and negative opinions. A semi-experiment with 50 participants revealed that keystroke patterns could differentiate opinions with accuracy above random guessing. A second approach using self-reported pleasure and arousal labels showed more accurate results, suggesting keystroke dynamics can identify sentiment but may benefit from multimodal integration.

research.problem: Analyzing behavioral patterns in human-computer interaction, specifically keystroke dynamics for sentiment classification.
research.motivation: Behavioral biometrics and physiological data are used in security and emotion recognition, but keystroke dynamics offer non-intrusive, hardware-free insights into user states.
research.objective: Differentiate positive and negative opinions using keystroke dynamics and assess the effectiveness of self-reported emotional labels.
research_questions: Is there a difference in keystroke dynamics patterns while writing positive and negative opinions?

methodology.summary: Keystroke dynamics features (digraphs, trigraphs, frequency, typing speed) were extracted from 50 participants' opinion-writing sessions using a 3s idle threshold for segmentation.
datasets: Keystroke data from 50 participants writing about learning experiences
preprocessing: Timestamp alignment with local computer time
methodology.training_strategy: Classification using self-reported emotional states as labels

experiments.experimental_setup: Semi-experiment with 50 participants writing opinions on best/worst learning experiences, with keystroke data captured during task execution.
experiments.results: Classification accuracy exceeded random guessing levels; self-reported pleasure/arousal labels improved accuracy.

performance.accuracy: Slightly above random guess level; more accurate with self-reported labels

contributions: Demonstrated feasibility of keystroke dynamics for sentiment classification
Highlighted value of multimodal integration for improved accuracy
limitations: Limited generalizability due to homogeneous sample
future_work: Multimodal approaches combining keystroke dynamics with physiological data
analysis.research_gap: Linking opinion content to emotional states without explicit emotional elicitation

sections.introduction: Focuses on behavioral biometrics in HCI, emphasizing keystroke dynamics as a source of emotional state information.
sections.related_work: Reviews keystroke dynamics applications in emotion recognition, user authentication, and mood monitoring.
sections.methodology: Details feature extraction from keystroke data and statistical analysis of emotional state correlations.
sections.results: Reports classification accuracy above random guessing and differential patterns between positive/negative opinions.
sections.discussion: Analyzes implications for affective computing and limitations of unimodal keystroke-based approaches.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes the potential of keystroke dynamics for sentiment analysis and the need for multimodal integration.

metadata.title: Under Pressure: Sensing Stress of Computer Users

abstract: Recognizing when computer users are stressed can help reduce their frustration and prevent negative health conditions. This work explores using pressure-sensitive keyboards and capacitive mice to detect stress through behavioral changes during tasks like typing and mouse clicking.

research.problem: Measuring stress non-invasively and continuously in work environments remains challenging.
research.motivation: To mitigate chronic stress-related health issues and improve human-computer interaction by detecting stress states.
research.objective: Evaluate if pressure-sensitive keyboards and capacitive mice can distinguish between stressful and relaxed conditions.
research_questions: Do stressed users exhibit distinct behavioral patterns with input devices?
Can device usage metrics reliably indicate stress states?

methodology.summary: A within-subjects laboratory study with 24 participants performing tasks under controlled stress and relaxed conditions, measuring typing pressure and mouse contact.

experiments.experimental_setup: Participants completed 30-minute sessions with stress-inducing tasks (e.g., timed typing, provocative text) and relaxed tasks, using pressure-sensitive keyboards and capacitive mice.
experiments.results: 79% of participants showed increased typing pressure, 75% exhibited more mouse surface contact during stress conditions.

contributions: Non-intrusive stress detection using existing input devices
Link between physiological stress and behavioral metrics
analysis.research_gap: Need for robust, scalable solutions for diverse work environments

sections.introduction: Describes stress's physiological impacts and the need for continuous, non-invasive stress detection to prevent health issues.
sections.related_work: Reviews stress measurement approaches, including physiological sensors, self-reports, and behavioral proxies like keyboard/mouse usage.
sections.methodology: Details the lab study design, input devices, tasks, and data collection procedures for stress state analysis.
sections.results: Presents statistical findings on typing pressure and mouse contact differences between stress and relaxed conditions.
sections.discussion: Analyzes implications for affective computing and limitations in real-world applicability.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes the potential of input device metrics for stress detection and recommendations for future research.

metadata.title: The Effect of Emotion on Keystroke: An Experimental Study Using Facial Feedback Hypothesis
metadata.venue: 35th Annual International Conference of the IEEE EMBS

abstract: The study investigates emotion recognition via keystroke dynamics using facial feedback. It validates differences in typing patterns under positive and negative emotional states through controlled experiments, supporting the development of non-intrusive emotion detection technologies.

research.problem: Computers lack understanding of user emotional states, leading to poor interaction experiences.
research.motivation: Develop non-intrusive emotion recognition methods to improve human-computer interaction.
research.objective: Validate differences in keystroke patterns between emotional states using facial feedback.
research_questions: Does facial feedback induce measurable changes in keystroke dynamics?

methodology.summary: Facial feedback was used to induce emotions, with keystroke duration and latency analyzed via t-tests.
datasets: 15 university students typing '67829751' under facial feedback conditions

experiments.experimental_setup: Subjects typed sequences under 'teeth' (positive) and 'lip' (negative) conditions with 30-second breaks. Data collected via C# software.
baselines: Previous studies on keystroke-based emotion recognition
experiments.results: Significant differences in duration and latency across emotional states (p<0.05).

contributions: Validates emotion-keystroke dynamics correlation via controlled experiments
advantages: Non-intrusive, low-cost method for emotion detection
future_work: Expand to diverse populations and real-world applications
analysis.research_gap: Limited controlled studies on emotion-keystroke relationships

sections.introduction: Emotion's role in human-computer interaction and limitations of current emotion recognition technologies.
sections.related_work: Existing methods using facial expressions, speech, and physiological data.
sections.methodology: Facial feedback induction, keystroke data collection, and statistical analysis.
sections.results: Statistically significant differences in keystroke duration/latency between emotional states.
sections.discussion: Implications for non-intrusive emotion recognition and limitations of individual variability.

metadata.title: A Review of Emotion Recognition Methods From Keystroke, Mouse, and Touchscreen Dynamics

abstract: This paper reviews state-of-the-art emotion recognition methods from keystroke, mouse, and touchscreen (KMT) dynamics, identifies key challenges, and outlines future research directions. It addresses six research questions regarding elicitation methods, recognizable emotions, features, classification techniques, application trends, and critical contexts.

research.problem: Accurately recognizing emotional states from non-intrusive KMT dynamics data.
research.motivation: Emotion recognition improves work performance and mental health by enabling emotion regulation, particularly in remote collaboration scenarios.
research.objective: Systematically review KMT-based emotion recognition methods, identify research gaps, and propose future directions.
research_questions: What are common emotion elicitation methods and databases?
Which emotions can be recognized from KMT dynamics?
What features are most suitable for specific emotions?
Which classification methods are most effective?
What are application trends of KMT-based emotion recognition?
Which application contexts are most critical?

methodology.summary: Systematic literature review using Web of Science and Google Scholar, filtering 142 articles to 102 relevant papers on KMT dynamics for emotion recognition.
preprocessing: Data filtering for relevant KMT dynamics

contributions: Systematic review of 20-year KMT-based emotion recognition literature
Answers to six research questions on elicitation, features, and applications
Identification of key research gaps and future directions
advantages: Non-intrusive data collection from KMT dynamics
limitations: Lack of detailed performance metrics in reviewed studies
analysis.research_gap: Need for more detailed reviews of advanced KMT dynamics methods

sections.introduction: Defines emotion as a multidimensional response to stimuli, emphasizing its role in work performance and mental health. Highlights KMT dynamics as non-intrusive data sources for emotion recognition.
sections.related_work: Summarizes existing reviews on facial expressions, physiological signals, and voice/text analysis, noting gaps in KMT dynamics research.
sections.methodology: Describes systematic review process, search strategies, and article filtering criteria to identify relevant KMT-based emotion recognition studies.
sections.results: Analyzes 102 papers on KMT dynamics, categorizing emotion elicitation methods, features, and classification approaches.
sections.discussion: Evaluates strengths and limitations of KMT-based emotion recognition, emphasizing its potential in remote collaboration and mental health applications.
sections.conclusion: Reiterates the importance of KMT dynamics for non-intrusive emotion recognition and outlines priorities for future research.

metadata.title: Identify user features impacting keystroke, mouse and touchscreen dynamics

abstract: The paper investigates how user features influence behavioral changes in keystroke, mouse, and touchscreen (KMT) dynamics, linking these to emotional states. It proposes a framework for personalized emotion recognition by identifying key user features and KMT dynamics features through questionnaire surveys and data analysis.

research.problem: Understanding how user features affect emotional changes via behavioral patterns in KMT dynamics.
research.motivation: Existing emotion recognition methods lack personalization due to insufficient consideration of user features.
research.objective: Identify key user and KMT dynamics features for personalized emotion recognition and develop a guiding framework.
research_questions: Which user features significantly impact KMT dynamics?
How do these features influence behavior qualitatively and quantitatively?
What framework supports personalized emotion recognition?

methodology.summary: A questionnaire survey with 107 participants and data analysis to explore relationships between user features and KMT dynamics features.
features: Gender, KMT proficiency, language proficiency, hand habit, software proficiency, task urgency, emotion
Typing speed, typing error rate, key pressure, mouse movement speed, clicking speed, clicking strength, keystroke speed
preprocessing: Feature selection from literature review and survey data

experiments.experimental_setup: Questionnaire survey with 107 participants to analyze user features' impact on KMT dynamics.
experiments.results: Identified seven key user features and seven KMT dynamics features for emotion recognition.

contributions: Identification of key user features influencing KMT dynamics
Key KMT dynamics features for emotion recognition
advantages: Non-intrusive KMT dynamics for emotion prediction
limitations: Emotion as a user feature remains unexplored
future_work: Deeper exploration of KMT dynamics-user feature relationships
analysis.research_gap: Lack of integration between emotion and user features in existing studies

sections.introduction: Discusses behavior-emotion distinction and the role of KMT dynamics in affective computing.
sections.related_work: Reviews studies on gender, age, handedness, and education level correlations with KMT dynamics.
sections.methodology: Describes survey-based data collection and analysis to identify feature relationships.
sections.results: Presents identified key user and KMT dynamics features for emotion recognition.
sections.discussion: Analyzes implications of findings for personalized emotion recognition frameworks.
sections.conclusion: Summarizes contributions and highlights research gaps in user feature integration.
